Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC (happy to adjust):

1) Goal: validate that Redwood can deliver consistent, high-quality product-recommendation snippets across web chat and mobile support channels with <150ms median latency and >=92% accuracy on a curated QA set.

2) Success criteria (proposal):
- Functional: top-1 recommendation relevance >= 92% on 500-sample test set (mix of English/Spanish/French).
- Latency: p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 450ms during simulated peak traffic (burst to 50 RPS).
- Stability: no more than 1% request failures during a 4-hour soak test.
- Cost target: inferred average token cost within our estimate (we'll provide an expected budget ceiling).

3) Scope & timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): share sample data, sign simple POC MSA (two-way NDA + scope).
- Week 1: environment setup (Redwood hosted POC tenant + model roster deployment), baseline evaluation on your samples.
- Week 2: tuning and prompt templates, run evaluation harness, interim sync.
- Week 3: soak test at scale + final report + next-step recommendation.

4) Model shortlist & fallback idea (high-level):
- Primary candidates: Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized), LLaMA-2-13B (q4) for higher quality.
- Fallback: a smaller quantized 7B or a distilled low-latency variant to keep tail latencies predictable if capacity is constrained.

5) Data: please share ~500 representative chat lines and any reranking labels you have (CSV is fine). See attachment: sample_user_messages.csv (placeholder).

6) Next steps: If this plan looks good, can we lock a start date for Monday 22 Mar? Also, can you confirm the language mix (EN/ES/FR) and whether PHI or payment data is present?

I've attached a short POC checklist and a draft evaluation rubric. I cc'd Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (product) to advise on model choices and metrics.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Thanks Priya — quick recommendations below. I put estimated p50/p95 numbers based on our hosted POC config (8xA10G burst-capable pool) and q4 quantization where noted. I'll update the Model_Roster_Recommendations.xlsx and drop to the Drive folder.

Model roster (primary / secondary / fallback):
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4) — good balance of instruction-following for short-form recommendations, best cost-performance for multilingual smaller contexts. Estimated latency p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms at 50 RPS burst with continuous batching.
- Secondary: LLaMA-2-13B (q4) — stronger reasoning on edge cases and slightly better cross-lingual quality for FR; latency p50 ~ 180ms, p95 ~ 520ms. Use when quality delta matters (selected queries).
- Fallback: QLoRA-distilled-7B (aggressive quant, q4_0) — very low latency, lower quality. Trigger rules: automatic routing when p95 > 600ms or when queued requests exceed configured concurrency threshold; also available as a cost-saver for low-priority background tasks.

Evaluation plan (high level):
1) Data prep: canonicalize sample_user_messages.csv into 3 language buckets; label gold responses for 500 evaluation samples (we can assist for 50 samples).
2) Baseline run: run each model on entire eval set; capture relevance, BLEU-ish metrics, and human preference on a 5-point scale for a 100-sample holdout.
3) Latency soak: replay traffic at increasing RPS (10/25/50) for a 4-hour window; measure p50/p95 and error rate.
4) A/B prompts: run 3 prompt templates (concise, contextual, clarification-first) and surface best-performing template per language.
5) Deliverable: short report with recommended model, runbook for production routing, and cost projection.

Owners (suggested):
- Priya: POC kickoff, procurement SOW, calendar invites.
- Marissa: model roster, evaluation harness, interim report (week 2).
- Karthik: prompt templates and mapping to product requirements, final recommendation.

I'll attach the XLSX with cost estimates and rough token math. If they prefer a single multilingual model, we should start with Mistral-Instruct and evaluate the L2-13B only for a small subset where we need higher cross-lingual fidelity.

-Marissa
